text_fidelity_a:
BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer) Mattel has brought a new world to target practice and just plain fun with soft dart guns with this BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster. With no batteries required, the fun is endless. Instead of batteries to power the gun, it is air powered. You have to pump the gun to get enough air pressure to fire the soft darts. Mattel states the gun is for ages 6 and up, but this gun is on the heavy side and requires a bit of strength just to pump it, so I feel ages 7 and up would be a better fit. Even though our 6 year old neighbor didn't want to put this gun down, it was difficult for him to pump it for firing.

The gun is very sturdy being large and made of a heavy plastic. I can see this gun lasting quite a bit of use and not ending up in the trash for a long while. Once pumped it is easy to fire, whether firing one dart or the entire 20 dart clip. At the end of the gun is a special shield you can open up to not only protect yourself from oncoming darts, but your opponents darts will actually stick to this protective shield, allowing you to capture his darts.

Besides the gun there are 30 Smart Stick darts, a 20 dart clip and a Smart Stick target included. The target is great for improving your aim, especially firing one dart at a time. The 20 dart clip is really fun, whether firing at the target or your opponent, as it fires all 20 darts in a matter of a few seconds. It literally fires up to 50 feet, as we shot all 20 darts and several darts went well over 45 feet away. The rapid fire at such a distance is really a lot of fun for the backyard.

Even though these darts are really soft plastic, you will find out that once the children find out how much fun it is to shoot darts at both the target and each other, you may want to purchase the safety eye gear. I don't know if having all 20 darts coming at you from 50 feet away would need some type of eye protection, but I feel it's better to have some type of eye gear on. There is no doubt, this is a safe, sturdy toy with your children wanting to run around and play with this outdoors, gives it 5 Stars. Just getting the kids off the couch away from video games makes it a 5 Star toy, as the exercise alone is worth 5 Stars.
text_fidelity_b: BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Sherlock Holmes Consulting Detective: Jack the Ripper & West End Adventures Standalone Game The predecessor to this game, Sherlock Holmes: Consulting Detective, is my all-time favorite game, and holds a high place on my game shelf despite being a “one and done” experience. Does this new iteration hold up to the high standard the previous game established?

To start with, the production value on this new version is heads and shoulders above the 2013 edition of SHCD that I own. The paper is printed on much nicer stock, the box is thicker and better designed to hold the contents, and the instruction manual in particular shows a great attention to detail that the previous edition lacked. I particularly like that in this edition, the solutions to each case are printed upside down in the back of the box, and that the solutions are encased in an envelope secured to each case book to prevent spoiling any aspects of the story with erroneous page turns.

Like the previous game, this “board game” is much more of a “choose your own adventure” story for you and your friends to solve. Each case is represented by a book, in which you’re given an introductory story, and then allowed free reign to investigate a variety of leads and allies to assist you in gathering information about whodunit. Once you think you know what’s happening, turn to the questions and find out what happened in this story – don’t worry, there are significant explanations and story to give closure to each case.

This is a stand-alone game, meaning that if you haven’t already played the original SHCD, you can purchase this with no strings attached. I don’t think I would recommend that for new players, however.

Jack the Ripper and the West End Adventures are quite different from what you get in the original game. In the original, there were some threads of story that remained from one case to the next, but in the new version, four of the cases are designed to be played campaign-style in an effort to solve the Jack the Ripper murders.

I’m sure that there will be many people out there who love the Jack the Ripper campaign - a set of four cases that are thematically tied together that will allow you to hunt down Jack using a separate map and additional investigative helpers – but it really isn’t for me. First of all, the cases are quite a bit darker and less whimsical than your traditional Sherlock Holmes story and case, and are tied together only by the fact that they occur in the same area and time period. I think the original cases are too difficult to be played by, let’s say, a 10 year old, but the stories wouldn’t be inappropriate for them in terms of language and description. The Jack cases, on the other hand, would carry a definite R-rating – they’re well-researched historically, and include lots of graphic description and a few cuss words as well. If you know anything about the historical Jack cases, you’d probably know this going in, but if you’re used to the style of the original cases, know that this is a darker affair. Secondly, you absolutely cannot find Jack and get a satisfactory conclusion until the fourth case, which is a decent investment in time with little return for parts 1 - 3. Third, and this is the big reason I didn’t like it, is that the mini-mysteries you’re solving in parts 1, 2 and 3 are not mysteries at all, but historical backstory. The questions are answered directly by particular sources, so if you visit the right allies and pursue the right leads you will simply be given the correct answers to each piece without putting much of anything together outside of remembering what the leads gave you. This was a very different experience, with a different writing style, different thematic elements, and a wholly different style, and since I am such a fan of the tried-and-true SHCD formula, I did not enjoy it as much as others may.

The other six cases are all stand-alone cases, and are quite good, although in most cases, they’re quite a bit harder than the already difficult cases in the original box. Like that set, some are better than others, but I will admit that the overall quality of these cases is on-par with what came in the original box, but still harder. I don’t think this is the right place to start with the SHCD universe.

Therein lies the only real problem that I have with this SHCD set – that while packaged as a stand-alone, this game is put together in a way that strongly suggests that it’s a sequel. If you think of it in movie terms, sure, you can watch most sequels without seeing the original movies, but why would you, especially if you know going in that watching the original is going to improve your experience? The cases in this box are more difficult, and the Jack the Ripper set is an odd starting place.

Overall, this game comes very highly recommended to any fan of the original set of cases. If this game sounds like something you’d be interested in, get it, but be advised that I think that the original set of 10 cases are a superior starting place.

4.5/5
text_fidelity_b: Sherlock Holmes Consulting Detective: Jack the Ripper & West End Adventures Standalone Game

text_fidelity_a:
Bezier Games America Board Game This is a nice game if you have tons of American trivia packed away in your brain, or if you'd like lots of it. The homeschool mama part of me likes that there's educational types of facts/questions included, like when was The Star Spangled Banner written and when the United States Senate first convened. There's also tons of "bubblegum" trivia, too, though, like the debut of Gilmore Girls and questions about Simcity. Those types are more abundant.

Each card will center around 3 topics: Year, State, and Number. For example, the card labeled Orange Julius will ask what year the first restaurant opened, what state has it as the World's Fair official beverage, and how many teaspoons of sugar are in a small orange julius. With this game, you can benefit even if you don't know the answer and guess close, which is good news for me!

As far as quality goes, this is a pretty nice game. The cards look nice, and have a picture of the subject on each one. They all follow the same format, which keeps things from getting confusing, and there's a huge variety of subjects. The board is thick cardboard, and the colored pieces are wooden blocks.

I really like how this is constructed. It's all wrapped in plastic, so there's no dangerous paper flap to cut open on the bottom of the box with a knife, and the puzzle is sealed inside in another bag, which prevents lost pieces. The pieces are thick and fit together well, and I really like the dark green backing that the pieces have. It looks really cool, and it makes it easy to see which pieces are upside down. The border is a graduated red/yellow, which makes it easy to separate out the edge pieces

Probably the reason I liked the puzzle most was that this puzzle makes you think and talk about fun memories, instead of just getting frustrated, trying to put 200 pieces of identical blue sky together, like some puzzles have.

This was a really fun puzzle to put together.

The Resistance (The Dystopian Universe) This game is addicting and so much fun for ages 10+. The teenagers at the summer camp I run especially found it fun.

The short version of how it works: Everyone gets an identity (spy or resistance member). Spies get to see who the other spies are, resistance members are clueless. You take turns choosing people to go on missions hoping that you don't have a spy among your group. Everyone on that mission turns in a pass or fail card. The spies are trying to get missions to fail, and resistance members are trying to pass the missions. You have 5 mission rounds to battle it out.

The first round or two playing with new people is always pretty quiet and awkward, but once everyone catches on to how to play, and opens up the game becomes a blast! It's been a great ice breaker for us, and it's got the kids talking and making friends with each other. All while being deceitful, calling others out for being spies, but overall having fun!

It's definitely more fun the more people you have, but it's still playable with only 5.
text_fidelity_b: The Resistance (The Dystopian Universe)

text_fidelity_a:
Hasbro Gaming Monopoly E Electronic Banking What can you possibly say new about Monopoly, the world's favorite property trading game, that hasn't already been said for decades since it's introduction by Parker Brothers in 1935? No matter what new version of Monopoly comes out, it's always so much fun to play with family and friends.

In the sixties, we always had one major problem when the entire family sat down to a long night of playing Monopoly, and that was, we always ran out of money if the game went on long enough. There used to be an office store named Burrows that sold extra Monopoly money and buying an extra packet or two was the only solution to our money shortage.

Now with this new version of Monopoly With Electronic Banking, you'll never run out of money, because there isn't any. The game comes with the standard board, dice, houses, hotels, Title Deed cards, Chance and Community Chest cards, 6 tokens and 6 bank cards that slide through an electronic banking unit which keeps track of your cash on your card. The electronic unit takes 2 AAA batteries (Not Included) and can store millions of dollars on each player's bank card.

It actually takes just as long to type in the money you accumulate on each player's card, as it does to hand count the cash to the players, so don't think this electronic unit is a time saver. We actually found when playing with 6 players, that it saved time to have a separate banker. This electronic banking version of Monopoly may not be faster than the cash version, but it's every bit as fun and that's saying a lot for a game that's been rated number one for over 75 years!

SwimSchool Baby Pool Float with Adjustable Canopy - 6-24 Months - Includes 5-Toy Interactive Play Console Safety Seat - Pink We like this "SwimSchool New Fabric Baby Pool Float, 6 - 24 Months, Berry/Pink." My 11 month old niece really loves this as it allows her to slowly move herself around the pool by kicking her legs. It fits her well and appears to be comfortable for her. It has two rings that are inflated with air with a seat in the center of the two rings and a moat of mesh fabric holding the two inflated rings together. The baby sits and the center with an additional strap between their legs that adjusts how deep in the water they are sitting. The baby can play with the water and water toys that are in the moat. This allows them to enjoy the water without the toys floating away or danger of the baby tipping.

The valves for inflating the rings are located in front of the baby, which seems a strange place to put them, but the tops do push in and tuck under a flap so that the baby can't easily pull them out. There is fabric over the inflated rings to protect them from damage, but you're warned to avoid using sharp objects near the rings. The rings are actually in a triangle shape with the point in front of the baby.

There is a awning that cannot be detached (as far as we can tell). It's supposed to be adjustable between three positions (behind the baby to above the baby), but we didn't have success in locking the awning in a certain position. And the awning is not big enough to really shade the baby very much. We would prefer to just remove the awning as we're using an indoor pool, but it does not come off. At least it is out the way, behind the baby. It comes with three scooping toys that somewhat float but mainly are fun shapes that can scoop and splash water.

The paint seems very thin, and flaked areas look like they'll easily spread with use. In many places, the paint came off when I peeled the part-number stickers off. I deducted the second star because the accessories were not as advertised in the listing or the video. Missing were the doghouse; one of the basketball standards (two were shown; only one was included); the bathroom sink; and one firefighter (two were included; the description promises three). The firefighter's helmet makes it nearly impossible for him to fit through the holes to slide down the pole. The Dalmatian dog pictured was replaced by a brown dog, with a dog bed that he does not fit into, instead of the doghouse. The included accessories match the parts-list in the instruction booklet, so I know the omissions were not accidental.

text_fidelity_a:
Marvel Guardians of The Galaxy Big Blastin' Rocket Raccoon Figure, 10 Inch I'm going to review this not from the perspective of a toy, but rather as a piece of movie memorabilia. Years ago, I use to love to go to the local mall here in Austin and stop by the SunCoast Motion Picture Company store. Where you could buy all sort of movie related items as well as the movies themselves. Over the years I've bought a number of items very similar to this Rocket Raccoon figure for my collection. So when I was offered one of these 10 inch figure to check out I gladly accepted.

I wasn't expecting this figure to be so big - I knew it was suppose to be 10" but it seems bigger than that to me. It came in one of those open face boxes that allow you to actually touch the toy before taking it out of the box, and you can activate the sound effect as the item ships with the batteries already installed and the sound box is set in a demo mode. The sounds it make are pretty loud, they should put a smile on any child face (and a frown on any adults in the room).

Once out of the box, there is some assembly required. You have to pop the tail into the figures rear-end (yeah, I know). It takes some effort to do that, so I suggest having an adult do it. Other than that, the figure is ready to go. Like I mentioned there is a demo mode on the effects box. The effects are controlled with a three-position switch - Off, Try Me (demo), and On. The unit is powered by three double-A batteries which are located in the figures backpack (there is a screw securing the cover to the batteries). Once you turn on the power switch, there are two activation points - one on the figures leg and another on top of the gun he is holding. Pressing one or the other activates both motion and sound effects, plus the figure speaks phrases from the movie. The motion effects are just the end of the gun rotating and the figure shaking a bit. There are some light effects with the end of the gun & gun sight lighting up. There aren't that many spoken phrases - so they can get a bit repetitive after awhile.

The toy is pretty well made - a lot more substantial than most of the movie memorabilia, but then again it was made for kids to play with.

I kept the figure on my desk at work for about a week before bringing it home. I can't tell you how times people stopped and played with the figure (too many times, as that is what prompted me to finally take it home). I haven't seen the movie yet - but it is definitely one that I plan on seeing this summer.

I really like this figure - about the only thing I could comment on would be the detail of the end of his gun, everything else has a decent level of detail, but that part of the gun doesn't. Guessing that is more due to the fact that they made it out of clear plastic so that the light effect could be seen.
text_fidelity_b: Marvel Guardians of The Galaxy Big Blastin' Rocket Raccoon Figure, 10 Inch

text_fidelity_a: Halloween Lights- 24 pcs Halloween LED Necklace Bracelets Pumpkin Ghost Pirate Spider Eyeball Necklace Halloween Party Favor Light up Flashing Decoration Trick Treats Gift Bag Fillers for Women Men Family Pack There are 24 different Halloween themed pieces in the box, ranging from pumpkins, to ghosts, to pirate ships, to spiders, to skulls.  The necklaces have a simple snap clasp at the end, and the bracelets have two different size settings.  The lights have three different colors including red, green, and blue.  There are three different setting to the lights with how they flash.  When first turned on, all three of the colors work great.  All the red, green and blue lights work at first.  But after about 10 minutes, the blue light starts to fade, then the green light starts to fade, until only the red light is working.  If turned off and left to sit and rest for a while, then all three light begin to light up and work again, but eventually again only the red light will remain lit.  This happened with all of the necklaces and bracelets in the box.  So as long as the lights are not needed to stay on for long periods of time, they are nice.  If needed for longer periods, two bracelets or necklaces or one of each could be used to alternate between them to give each one a rest by turning it off to refresh the colors.  So if handing these out for Halloween treats, I would recommend giving kids two in order to compensate for the lights not working all the time.

LEGO DUPLO Town Steam Train 10874 Remote Control Set - Learning Toy and Daycare Accessory for Toddlers, Boys, Girls, and Kids 2-5 Years Old, Push and Go Battery Powered Set with RC Function I really love these Duplo Lego sets. While I do not have any little ones in the house, I like having some toys on hand for the occasional visitors with kids. These are always a hit and now when friends with little ones come over, the kids always remember our place because of the "Lego Lady!" haha! Bringing out the Legos has brought shy little ones out of their shell as they put together the pieces and play away.

This train set is great! it is super simple to put together, as with any Duplo set. You will need to unscrew the battery box to put in 4 AAA batteries, though. If you're lazy like me and don't want to trudge out to the garage for a screwdriver, you can easily open it with a table knife (haha.. see pic). To make the train go, first be sure there are batteries installed and then push the on/off button on the bottom. put the train on the track. The wheels straddle the inner upright portions of the track (see pic). Then simply give the train a little push and off it goes around the track.

To control the train, use the little action tiles. These are flat pieces with a small icon on them. There is one for each of the following actions. When the train goes over it, it performs the action:
- whistle (yellow) makes a train whistle sound
- horn (white) makes one toot sound - I thought this was for the lights but those didnt come on when it went over this one
- water (blue) stops for a bit there and makes a sound like it is getting water for the steam engine
- reverse (green) stops and reverses the train
- stop (red) stops the train

The action bricks are really easy to put down on the track - they just lay in the middle of the track and don't actually attach. So it is easy for the little ones to pick them up and move them around. This is super fun for the kiddos and definitely keeps them happy occupied for quite some time!

There is an App you can get as well - works for iPhone, iPad, and Android devices. It has nothing to do with the train set itself, though. I thought maybe it did, but it is really just a separate app/Game. It is a fun little game for young kids, though. App Tip: if you have an iPhone and aren't getting any sound with the app, be sure you don't have the device on mute. (for iPhones it is that side button you switch on/off). I don't have an iPad but I suspect it could have the same issue.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO DUPLO Town Steam Train 10874 Remote Control Set - Learning Toy and Daycare Accessory for Toddlers, Boys, Girls, and Kids 2-5 Years Old, Push and Go Battery Powered Set with RC Function

text_fidelity_a:
Tapple - Fast Word Fun For Everyone This is an easy-to-learn game with minimal set-up. It’s fast-paced and the rounds and the games go quickly. The circular game board has letters from which to select and a 10-second time. A player draws a card and picks one of two categories to play, such as “Pizza Toppings”. The first player thinks of something that fits that category, such as “Cheese”, and presses the “C” on the board. The next player now needs to think of a pizza topping, but can’t use the letter “C”. Play continues until only one player remains. Then, the round is over and the next player chooses a card.

The game requires 2 “AA” batteries that are not included. There is a storage place on the bottom of the game board for the cards. If the timer wasn’t so loud, it would be a great game for the car. It would be good to bring on a trip to play once you arrived, since it’s compact with self-contained storage for the cards. This is a great game for families because the cards are double-sides with different difficulty levels on each side.

It was harder than it seems to come up with things that fit the category beginning with one of the available letters, within the time-limit. Younger kids may get bored after a few rounds, but great game for passing a short amount of time. It would be nice if it came with more cards, because if it did become a family favorite, it wouldn’t take long to go through the cards. Still, it’s a fun family game.
text_fidelity_b: Tapple - Fast Word Fun For Everyone

text_fidelity_a:
LEGO NINJAGO Temple of Resurrection 70643 Building Kit (765 Piece) What I like with this LEGO set is that it does come with 7 mini figures. Makes it so much easier for me because I didn't have to run out to try to find some type of figures so the kids were able to play with this once they got it all built.
I let the older grandchildren go ahead and build this by themselves. It's getting hard for Paps to see all those smaller pieces anymore.
What was cute is that once they had it about 1/2 way built, they let the smaller kids pretend that the "warriors" were in command on getting their temple built. Because of that, they really helped keep the younger ones occupied for at least 3 days.
This is what I love about toys like this. Kids aren't glued to the tv, and kids aren't glued to their phones. They are using their brains and their hands to build something. Then they are using their brains to come up with a new adventure each time they play with it.
And, it's not set for just one age group. Yes, to build it the child has to be a certain age to understand the concept of putting it all together and reading the instructions. But, once it's all built the younger children (once they know not to put small items in their mouths or destroy what's built) can join in and play. Right now we have kids ranging from 4 1/2 to 12 playing with it. And when they grow older and lose interest in it, we pack up the entire set in zip baggies, add the instructions, and repack it into the box to save for the next generation of kids in the future.
I have always liked how well LEGOS are made. Parts are nice and sturdy and the colors on the blocks seem to last for years on end.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO NINJAGO Temple of Resurrection 70643 Building Kit (765 Piece)

text_fidelity_a:
Mega Bloks Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles Sewer Lair Building Kit We're huge Lego fans in my house, so while it may not be fair, I couldn't help but compare Mega Bloks with Lego. We got a few kits to try out, but otherwise, we've only used Lego in the past(though quite a bit of it). Unfortunately, Mega Bloks has just fallen short, for me, and I wasn't overly impressed(for the most part).

First of all, I've been spoiled to numbered bags. While this kit is divided into separate bags, you have to open all of them and dump them out, because the pieces you need for each step could be in any of the bags. I prefer, if I'm using a kit, to have my steps divided by bags. It keeps thing from getting less jumbled and lost, and it provides great "rest" points. It kind of made me wonder what the point of all the bags were in this set.

Second, these blocks just didn't go together smoothly. Some of them require a great deal of pressure to get attached. They hurt my fingers. I even snapped my finger between two of the blocks at one point trying to get pieces together. (Sad, but true.) My fingers just ache after working with Mega Bloks due to the amount of pressure required to get some of the pieces together. Some of the pieces were incredibly frustrating to get together. Not only that but some of the parts from the final product keep falling off/apart. It took so long to put the thing together(with so much pain) that it almost brings some tears to see parts fall off. ;)

Third, the directions aren't as clear as I'd prefer. Sure, as an adult, I figured things out, but for the average child, the directions just make things harder than they have to be.

When I discovered that Mega Bloks were compatible with Lego, I was really excited. I thought that the block building world could open up to more options for me and my children. We're sticking with Lego, though! It seems more organized and the pieces are more reliable. (They have more of a perfect fit than we've experienced with Mega Bloks.)

In defense of Mega Bloks, though, the little figurines are way cooler! IF you are a fan of Mega Bloks, this kit is cool! (I just found it a pain. Literally.)
text_fidelity_b: Mega Bloks Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles Sewer Lair Building Kit

Abacus Brands Virtual Reality World Atlas - Illustrated Interactive VR Atlas and STEM Learning Activity Set This is a cool concept, and the app is easy enough to install and setup. I guess the only thing I was disappointed in, was that I was hoping to discover at least a few magical immersive experiences. Like visiting a pyramid in Egypt, for example. But instead, these are all short videos that have a broader and less immersive look into the different places. In Egypt for example, you visit Cairo and see pyramids, but you don’t get to see inside of the pyramids. The videos are all broad strokes of places or animals. Which I guess in some ways make sense, as it’s an atlas. However, it would have been so magical to at least have some really cool immersive experiences.

Overall, it’s a cool educational toy/gadget. But it could have been so much cooler, in my opinion.

text_fidelity_a: Disney and Pixar WALL-E Robot Toy, Remote Control Hello WALL-E Robot Figure, Gifts for Kids (Amazon Exclusive) Remote control Wall-E is a great toy! It doesn’t go racing as fast as a car so it’s easier to control, especially for younger kids. The left button on the remote makes him go forward, and the right button puts him in reverse at a slight turn so you can maneuver his position.  His eyes light up blue and he moves his arms up and down. You can manually open and close his hands. He says his name, and makes other garbage/industrial type of noises. His volume is a little on the loud side for me, so I will probably put a little tape over the sound box. Wall-E came with batteries installed, but the remote needed 3 AAA batteries. text_fidelity_a: MONOPOLY: Fortnite Edition Board Game Inspired by Fortnite Video Game Ages 13 & Up This version of Monopoly does not use money! Genius idea for very little children! Even my 4-year-old loved playing. It can be very quick (which was perfect!). I was out before I ever passed Go, haha. Instead of money, this game uses green circles called HP. You gradually lose them all to the “bank” in the middle, but you can get more by passing Go or by landing on a plus-one space or by drawing a particular card. When you land on an available property, it’s yours for free. If you land on an owned property, you have to pay a green HP. Simple. This game is easy to understand, super fun, and quick for the short attention spans of young Fortnite players. Instead of everyone starting on Go, we all started on a homemade Battle Bus, jumping off and landing on whatever space you want. So we all started the game in different areas of the board and all started with a property. That helped the game go faster and was just plain fun to copy Fortnite. Hape Quadrilla Wooden Marble Run Construction - Vertigo - Quality Time Playing Together Safe and Smart Play for Smart Families,Multicolor This is one of those toys that can provide HOURS of entertainment AND education. You're working those brain cells to build these railways! There's a booklet included with lots of different railways to build. It gives you step by step instructions by picture. You DO have to pay close attention to what color block you place where, and where the holes line up, and how many blocks you use. It all has to line up just right. That said, I wouldn't call this a difficult toy at all. It *will* exercise the mind, though.

I like using it with my 5 year old. It's helping him to follow directions. Of course, I still have to help a great deal. It's also helping him with counting, which he struggles with. It's helping my 2 year old learn his colors. Plus, we're ALL learning patience! ;) These railways fall down pretty easily, since it's basically stacking blocks on top of each other. Honestly, for most 2-3 year olds, I think this thing probably isn't the best idea just yet. For older children, it's wonderful. It has potential to grow with them for *years* to come. This is fun for adults, too! I've had a blast with it.

My ONLY complaint with this thing is the fact that the marbles have nothing to catch them as the come out of the final holes/blocks. They just roll away. We have a 7 month old that crawls everywhere and puts everything in his mouth. We're always careful, but playing with this thing, we have to be extraordinarily careful, especially due to the free rolling marble issue. So far, we haven't came up with a "catching place" for those last marbles, but I'm sure we will in time. We just can't use all the marbles at one time, and keep a close count on what we do use.

The extra caution we have to use is WELL worth it, though!!

This is the kind of toy you just can't go wrong with! (Unless you have children that might choke on those marbles...use your best judgment at that point). Highly recommended from us!

text_fidelity_a: Nature Gift Store Kids Worm Farm Observation Kit Shipped with Live Worms I ordered this as a Christmas gift for my young daughter who is into all things worms, gardening, and composting. It estimated it would arrive December 5th, but it arrived a lot earlier. I think earlier shipping is always fine with the exception of live creatures. Being more than a month away, I was worried the worms wouldn't make it for the holidays. I contacted the seller right away to get tips on how to keep the worms alive and they were not helpful at all. I think I got a one or two sentence reply with no information. So I decided to do some research myself and I was able to keep them all alive without having to transfer them until the farm was opened on Christmas day. I kept them in the dark and a cool area of my house. I would take the cup out once a week to check on them. I'd water the soil a little every other week (just moist, not wet). I also set a couple carrot shavings, a torn up spinach leaf, and a broken egg shell on the top.  The worms did really well.  We transferred them as soon as she opened the farm.  The farm itself was disappointing in size and much smaller than I was expecting. It's more like the size of holding your two hands side by side. We plan to transfer them from the farm to her vermicompost bin in a few weeks.  She seems happy with the purchase, but overall I would not recommend this farm and would suggest creating your own with a little more research.
text_fidelity_b: Nature Gift Store Kids Worm Farm Observation Kit Shipped with Live Worms

text_fidelity_a:
Evviva Ant Habitat W/LED Light. Enjoy A Magnificent Habitat. Great for Kids & Adults. Evviva Ant Ecosystem W/Enhanced Blue Gel. Educational & Learning Science Kit. Live Ants Not Included This ant farm was a fascinating gift for everyone, not just the 6 year old who got it. We ordered the ants from AntsAlive .com and when they arrived they quickly scurried about, digging their first hole within a few hours. Before you add the ants, you must poke 3 to 4 holes in the gel to help the ants get started. I’m wondering if the negative reviews forgot this step, leaving the ants confused in the farm on where they could go.

I highly recommend refrigerating the ants for 10 minutes before you add them to the farm so they don’t immediately escape. I also highly recommend putting them in on the side nearest the white air hole plug. Inevitably a few ants will have died in shipment and it’s much easier to remove them through the hole then removing the entire lid (as others will try to escape).

Why this ant farm is better than others?
1) The ants food and water supply is in the gel. Other ant farms require food and water be added for the ants; adding too much can create mold or too little and the ants are hungry. It’s challenging to calculate and extra work.

2) The glass is fairly narrow front to back so it’s likely the ants (as they did for us) will dig right to the class so you can see them clearly while they work under ground.

3) The light and magnifying glass make it very easy to see every ant at work.

4) The farm is reusable. You can clean out the old gel and ants and buy new ants and gel for a second use.

I highly recommend this gift for any child aged 4-10. Certainly older children and adults will enjoy it too.

*The attached photos are of the ant farm on day 3.

text_fidelity_b: Evviva Ant Habitat W/LED Light. Enjoy A Magnificent Habitat. Great for Kids & Adults. Evviva Ant Ecosystem W/Enhanced Blue Gel. Educational & Learning Science Kit. Live Ants Not Included

LeapFrog My Pal Violet (Frustration Free Packaging) Three of my four kids have had a LeapFrog My Pal Scout or Violet. Our first born would have had one but I don't think they were made back then. These little interactive toys are so great! Here's why I think your little ones will love them too!

1) It doesn't just talk, Scout/Violet says your child's name, puts their name into songs, and engages the child on a personal level. As soon as my kids realized it was talking to them they would laugh and try to make it do it again. It is still their favorite feature.
2) You can further personalize the Scout/Violet to sing/talk about your child's favorite animal, food and color. The pup uses these favorite things in silly songs. Warning: they are catchy and you will get them stuck in your head!
3) When your child changes, so does Scout/Violet. Anytime the favorites change you can just set the pup to match. The cord to plug it into your computer (USB) is housed right in the back of the pup. Once upon a time the cord was not attached. Be thankful it can't get lost with these newer models.
4) It plays "Bedtime Music" to which you can decide how many minutes it will play. My kids don't sleep to music so we've never used this feature officially, but they still like to press the paw and turn it on and off and on and off and on and off.

I would recommend this to babies 6+ months up to 2 years. My daughter is almost 4 and still plays with hers, but she's really too old for it now.
text_fidelity_b: LeapFrog My Pal Violet (Frustration Free Packaging)
